Ibn Sa'di's commentary on surah 80, verses 11–32:

{11–16} He, exalted is He, says: {Nay! Indeed, it is a reminder}: that is, truly, this admonition is a reminder from God, by which He reminds His servants, and He makes clear in His Book what they need, and He makes clear right guidance (rushd) from error (ghayy). When this has become clear, {whoever wills may remember it}: that is, act upon it, as in His saying: {And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve."} Then He mentions the place of this reminder, its greatness, and the elevation of its rank, saying: {In scriptures honored, exalted, purified}: exalted in rank and standing, purified from defects and from the hands of the devils reaching it or stealing it; rather, it is {in the hands of scribes}: they are the angels, who are envoys between God and His servants, {noble, righteous}: that is, abundant in goodness and blessing, and pure in their hearts and deeds. All of this is a protection from God for His Book, in that He made the envoys who carry it to the Messengers noble, powerful, pious angels, and did not give the devils any way over it. This is among the things that necessitate belief in it and receiving it with acceptance.

{17–23} Yet despite this, man refuses except disbelief. For this reason He, exalted is He, says: {Woe to man! How ungrateful he is!}: toward the blessing of God, and how fierce is his opposition to the truth after it has become clear. And what is he? He is among the weakest of things. God created him from a base fluid, then decreed his creation and fashioned him as a proportioned human, and perfected his outward and inward faculties. {Then He made the way easy for him}: that is, He facilitated for him the religious and worldly means, guided him to the path, made it clear to him, and tested him with commands and prohibitions. {Then He causes him to die and buries him}: that is, He honored him with burial, and did not make him like the rest of the animals whose carcasses lie on the face of the earth. {Then, when He wills, He will raise him up again}: that is, He will resurrect him after his death for recompense. God alone is the One who manages man and turns him through these changes; no partner shares with Him in this. Yet despite all this, man does not perform what God has commanded him, and does not fulfill what He has obligated upon him, but remains forever negligent, still under obligation!

{24–32} Then God guided him to reflect and contemplate on his food, and how it reaches him after passing through many stages, which God facilitated for him. He says: {Let man look at his food. That We pour down the water, pouring it abundantly}: that is, We send down rain upon the earth in abundance. {Then We split the earth, splitting it} for vegetation. {And We cause to grow therein}: varieties classified into kinds of delicious foods and desirable sustenance, {grain}: and this includes all grains of their various kinds, {and grapes and herbage}: which is fodder, {and olives and palm trees}: He singled out these four for the abundance of their benefits and uses, {and gardens of dense trees}: that is, orchards containing many intertwined trees, {and fruit and pasture}: fruit is what a person enjoys eating, such as figs, grapes, peaches, pomegranates, and others. Pasture is what cattle and livestock eat. For this reason He says: {as provision for you and your livestock}: which God created and subjected for you. Whoever contemplates these blessings, this should compel him to thank his Lord, to exert effort in turning to Him, to devote himself to His obedience, and to affirm His reports.

All of this is a protection from God for His Book, in that He made the envoys who carry it to the Messengers noble, powerful, pious angels, and did not give the devils any way over it. This is among the things that necessitate belief in it and receiving it with acceptance.

{17–23} Yet despite this, man refuses except disbelief. For this reason He, exalted is He, says: {Woe to man! How ungrateful he is!}: toward the blessing of God, and how fierce is his opposition to the truth after it has become clear. And what is he? He is among the weakest of things. God created him from a base fluid, then decreed his creation and fashioned him as a proportioned human, and perfected his outward and inward faculties. {Then He made the way easy for him}: that is, He facilitated for him the religious and worldly means, guided him to the path, made it clear to him, and tested him with commands and prohibitions. {Then He causes him to die and buries him}: that is, He honored him with burial, and did not make him like the rest of the animals whose carcasses lie on the face of the earth. {Then, when He wills, He will raise him up again}: that is, He will resurrect him after his death for recompense. God alone is the One who manages man and turns him through these changes; no partner shares with Him in this. Yet despite all this, man does not perform what God has commanded him, and does not fulfill what He has obligated upon him, but remains forever negligent, still under obligation!

{24–32} Then God guided him to reflect and contemplate on his food, and how it reaches him after passing through many stages, which God facilitated for him. He says: {Let man look at his food. That We pour down the water, pouring it abundantly}: that is, We send down rain upon the earth in abundance. {Then We split the earth, splitting it} for vegetation. {And We cause to grow therein}: varieties classified into kinds of delicious foods and desirable sustenance, {grain}: and this includes all grains of their various kinds, {and grapes and herbage}: which is fodder, {and olives and palm trees}: He singled out these four for the abundance of their benefits and uses, {and gardens of dense trees}: that is, orchards containing many intertwined trees, {and fruit and pasture}: fruit is what a person enjoys eating, such as figs, grapes, peaches, pomegranates, and others. Pasture is what cattle and livestock eat. For this reason He says: {as provision for you and your livestock}: which God created and subjected for you. Whoever contemplates these blessings, this should compel him to thank his Lord, to exert effort in turning to Him, to devote himself to His obedience, and to affirm His reports.

{33–42} That is: when the Blast of the Resurrection comes, by whose terror the ears are deafened and the hearts are stirred, on that Day—because of the terrors people will see and their dire need for the deeds they sent ahead—a person will flee from the dearest and most compassionate of people to him: from his brother, his mother, his father, his companion (i.e., his wife), and his children. That is because "for every person among them on that Day there will be a matter that occupies him" (80:37); that is, his own soul has preoccupied him, he is concerned with its release, and he has no attention for anything else. Then creation will divide into two groups: the happy and the wretched. As for the happy, their faces on that Day are "radiant" (80:38); that is, joy and delight have appeared in them because of what they have come to know of their deliverance and their success in attaining bliss, "laughing, joyful" (80:39). "And faces" of the wretched "on that Day will have upon them dust" (80:40); "darkness will cover them" (80:41), that is, they are overspread by it. So they are black, dark, and gloomy, having despaired of every good and recognized their wretchedness and ruin. "Those" who have this description "are the disbelievers, the wicked" (80:42); that is, those who disbelieved in the blessing of God, denied His signs, and dared to violate His sacred prohibitions. We ask God for pardon and well-being; indeed He is Generous and Bountiful.

And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.
